svg.title: One polygon function, four calls
svg.desc: An animation of an XRP seen from above with a marker in the hole between its wheels. Four buttons run the four calls from the lesson: polygon (4, 30), polygon (3, 30), polygon (6, 20) and polygon (8, 15). Each starts from the same mark, facing up, and draws its shape in blue, turning left at each corner, while a panel shows the call, the values sides and side_length take, and the turn the function works out: 360 divided by 4 is 90 degrees, a square; 360 divided by 3 is 120, a triangle; 360 divided by 6 is 60, a hexagon; 360 divided by 8 is 45, an octagon. Every shape ends back on its start mark, because the turns add up to 360 degrees.
